question.stem: Explain the security risk introduced by typing authority as AccountInfo instead of Signer<'info>.
question.explanation: AccountInfo does not enforce cryptographic signature verification, allowing any caller to pass an arbitrary public key and spoof the authority to withdraw funds.

rubric.name: Signer Verification
rubric.description: Explains that AccountInfo lacks signer verification allowing unauthorized callers to spoof authority

rubric.name: Security Impact
rubric.description: Explains fund theft or unauthorized withdrawal as the consequence

developer_answer: Typing authority as AccountInfo means Anchor does not verify that the account signed the transaction. An attacker can pass any public key as the authority and unauthorized callers can withdraw funds from the vault.
rationale: Developer accurately explains lack of signer verification and unauthorized withdrawal consequence.

question.stem: Explain why raw arithmetic operators like '+' must be replaced with checked methods in smart contracts.
question.explanation: Raw arithmetic operators can overflow or underflow. In release mode Rust may silently wrap integers causing balance inflation.

rubric.name: Overflow Hazard
rubric.description: Explains integer overflow and underflow risks in arithmetic operations

rubric.name: Checked Arithmetic
rubric.description: Recommends checked_add or saturating_add to prevent corrupted balances

developer_answer: Using raw plus arithmetic operator can cause integer overflow. In production builds, integer overflow wraps silently leading to corrupted balance calculations. Checked arithmetic like checked_add should be used instead.
rationale: Clear explanation of integer overflow, silent wrap hazard, and recommendation of checked_add.

question.stem: Explain why account realloc requires 'realloc::zero = true'.
question.explanation: Reallocating without zeroing can expose stale uninitialized memory from previous account allocations.

rubric.name: Memory Initialization
rubric.description: Explains memory zero initialization to prevent residual data leaks

rubric.name: Security Risk
rubric.description: Explains revival or stale data reading vulnerability

developer_answer: When an account is reallocated to a larger size, realloc::zero ensures the newly allocated memory bytes are zero initialized. Without zeroing, residual uninitialized data from previous accounts can be read.
rationale: Accurate explanation of zero initialization and residual memory leaks.

question.stem: Explain why floating-point division on lamports leads to bugs in Solana wallets.
question.explanation: Lamports are atomic integer units (u64). Floating-point division causes fractional lamport precision errors and transaction rejection on-chain.

rubric.name: Integer Invariant
rubric.description: Explains that lamports are discrete integers (u64) that cannot be fractional

rubric.name: Precision Loss
rubric.description: Explains JavaScript floating-point truncation and BigInt / BN requirement

developer_answer: Lamports on Solana are atomic integer units. Using JavaScript float division creates fractional lamport numbers with precision loss, causing transactions to fail because on-chain instructions require integer lamports. BigInt should be used.
rationale: Correctly highlights integer precision loss, fractional lamports, and BigInt solution.

rationale: Fails to recognize that fractional lamports are invalid on-chain.

question.stem: Explain the consequence of passing UI amount directly to createTransferInstruction without scaling by mint decimals.
question.explanation: SPL token instructions expect raw base units (e.g. 1 USDC = 10^6 base units). Passing unscaled UI amount transfers a tiny fraction of the intended tokens.

rubric.name: Decimal Scaling
rubric.description: Explains that on-chain token instructions require base units scaled by 10^decimals

rubric.name: Transfer Discrepancy

developer_answer: SPL token instructions require base units scaled by 10^decimals. If you pass raw UI amount to createTransferInstruction without decimal scaling, you transfer an unscaled fraction of what the user requested.
rationale: Explains SPL base units, decimal exponent scaling, and the discrepancy risk.
